item.title: Bridging the Gap: Extending a Static IP Office Network with a TP-Link C54
item.description:
Setting up network hardware usually feels like a plug-and-play affair. You unbox a router, plug in the WAN cable, and let DHCP handle the rest. It just works. But things get complicated when you are dealing with a static IP office environment. Honestly, bridging a fixed local area connection to a new Wi-Fi ecosystem requires a bit of manual maneuvering.

So, let’s walk through replacing an aging router and extending its reach using a TP-Link C54, keeping all the original credentials intact.

item.title: Configuring Browser Proxies and Bypassing Local DNS Restrictions for Sikkim Government Portals
item.description:
Navigating government portals often requires specific network configurations, particularly when local domain names rely on internal National Informatics Centre (NIC) DNS infrastructure. If you are accessing services like the Sikkim DDO Pranali portal (ddo.pranali.sikkim.nic.in) through a proxy setup, misconfigured DNS settings can lead to domain resolution failures or local DNS leaks.

This detailed guide breaks down how to configure system-wide and browser-specific proxies in Firefox and Opera, and how to set up FoxyProxy Standard to safely route NIC DNS traffic.

item.title: Troubleshooting Linux Mint Wi-Fi Drops: From Hardware Drivers to Automated NTP Time Sync
item.description:
Troubleshooting Linux Mint Wi-Fi Drops: From Hardware Drivers to Automated NTP Time Sync

Experiencing random Wi-Fi disconnections on Linux Mint—where the network suddenly drops and all available Wi-Fi access points disappear from the menu—is a surprisingly common frustration.

While this issue is often caused by aggressive driver power management or missing proprietary modules, another common underlying culprit is system clock drift. When your local system clock drifts out of alignment with remote authentication servers, security handshakes silently fail, dropping your wireless connection.

item.title: Troubleshooting Linux Time Synchronization: Fixing Systemd NTP, ISP Blocks, and Missing Daemons
